arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Boyce argued that Atlas' post-filing citizenship change should not create retroactive jurisdiction.
Mr. Greenberg argued that the trial court had jurisdiction because diversity existed at trial.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the timing of diversity jurisdiction. One side argues jurisdiction exists if diversity is present at trial. The other side argues jurisdiction must exist at filing.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Atlas argues that a post-filing citizenship change cures the lack of complete diversity.
Dataflux argues that a post-filing citizenship change cannot create retroactive diversity jurisdiction.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines when federal courts gain diversity jurisdiction. It determines whether parties can cure jurisdictional defects after filing. It affects access to federal courts for diverse parties.
